subject: linguistics
intro: Linguistics leads into the professions that work with language itself: interpreting, speech therapy, captioning, and the computational language work behind modern language models.

roles.title: Interpreters and Translators
roles.what: Interpret oral or sign language, or translate written text from one language into another — carrying meaning between speakers and texts in courts, hospitals, conferences and media while preserving register and intent.
roles.where: Phonetics and the IPA train you to hear and produce unfamiliar sound systems; morphology and syntax teach the structure you manipulate when converting between languages; the dialects unit covers the variation working interpreters navigate daily.

roles.title: Speech-Language Pathologists
roles.what: Assess and treat people with speech, language, voice and fluency disorders, select alternative communication systems and teach their use, and may perform research related to speech and language problems.
roles.where: The phonetics and phonology units give the transcription and sound-pattern analysis behind disorder assessment; the language-acquisition unit shows how children crack the code — the baseline for spotting when development diverges.

roles.title: Court Reporters and Simultaneous Captioners
roles.what: Use verbatim methods and equipment to capture, store, retrieve and transcribe pretrial and trial proceedings or other information; stenocaptioners operate computerised stenographic captioning equipment to caption live or prerecorded broadcasts for hearing-impaired viewers.
roles.where: Phonetics teaches you to segment continuous speech into the sounds a steno machine encodes; the phonology units' practice at spotting contrasts underlies captioning speech accurately in real time.

roles.title: Data Scientists
roles.what: Develop and implement techniques or analytics applications that transform raw data into meaningful information, applying data mining, data modelling, natural language processing and machine learning to large structured and unstructured datasets.
roles.where: Unit 12 extends the course into corpora and computational modelling of language and into how language technology becomes language models — the natural-language-processing pipeline data scientists build on top of linguistic structure.
